Cobaru's Aerie

Cobaru's Aerie is the gothic and luxurious apartment of Victae Cobaru, one of the city's secret vampires. Parties are frequently held in the apartment, satisfying their master's carnal desires and his hunger for blood, which he keeps fairly well in check by hiring merchants to obtain his meals legitimately.⁠

Shileh

Shileh is one of the numerous large, prosperous cities that dot the fertile Qadiran region of Pashman. It is located north of the banks of the Pashman River along Pashman's south-western border with the neighbouring region of Tapur.⁠⁠
49226950:
Zura's Mouth

Zura's Mouth is a series of springs and pools in the Kaava Lands and the source of the slow and broad Oubinga River which meanders through the jungles of the southwestern Mwangi Expanse before emptying into Desperation Bay. A number of tribes worship the place and use the pools for ritual sacrifice by drowning. The bodies don't last long, as the Oubinga's upper reaches are home to crimson maka-yika, a schooling, carnivorous fish similar to piranhas.⁠
49621200:
Rosehaven

Rosehaven is a small Galtan village located on the East Sellen River south of the River Kingdoms city of Liberthane. They celebrate an annual three-day autumn festival known as Mercylight, commemorating the community's defeat of a small coven of Gyronna-worshipers in 4684 AR.⁠⁠⁠
49753090:
Drowned Eye

The Drowned Eye, an underwater pit about four miles west of Acisazi, has long been regarded by the aquatic elves of that village as a cursed place. Its founders placed protective wards around the pit, and generations of elves avoided the area. Ironically, the notorious site's reputation has helped protect the village from outsiders.⁠
57028320:
Bellis

Bellis is a remote settlement in far northeastern Andoran along the banks of the Sellen River. Established as a lumber town, it now produces additional agricultural goods in addition to cut timber.⁠ Bellisians like to refer to themselves as "foresters" and regard "lumberjacks" as undisciplined amateurs.⁠

Diggen's Rest

Diggen's Rest is a watchtower in the Verduran Forest of eastern Andoran, north of the town of Fusil⁠⁠ and on the border between Andoran and Galt. It served as the final location of the records from Pathfinder lodges once founded by Kerinha Napsunar, one of the first Pathfinders.⁠
86512020:
Zhenbarghua

Zhenbarghua is the westernmost kuru settlement in the Cannibal Isles and maybe the least dedicated to the Blood Queen. Kuru from Zhenbarghua sometimes manage to escape their depraved culture and islands in search of a new life.⁠
89891810:
Gensmaren

The ruins of an ancient Taldan supply post, Gensmaren is located in the Vergan Forest of Razmiran and is now the lair of a stranded group of driders who try not to attract the attention of the local human authorities.⁠
97865140:
Brunderton

The mining town of Brunderton in eastern Rostland in Brevoy is home to a relatively large number of dwarves for the region. Most dwarves throughout southern Brevoy and the northern River Kingdoms have relatives from here, and gem and ore traders from Brunderton can often be found peddling their wares along the Sellen's many tributaries.⁠⁠⁠
108564540:
Te Taspeh Valley

Te Taspeh Valley is a peaceful land dotted with the ruins of ancient wooden homes believed to be the surviving remnants of Mendev's once-nomadic society. Unusual carvings associate these buildings with these ancient people, who were believed to settle only in locations of great spiritual importance.

As of 4725 AR the valley's ruins had yet to be investigated in large part due to the possessive behavior of a nearby adamantine dragon.⁠
113695970:
Counting House

The squat building of the Counting House served as the first moneylender in Kintargo and is located in the prosperous district known as The Greens.⁠⁠ As of 4724 AR, it now serves as a meeting hall for Silver Council meetings with members of Kintargo's aristocracy.⁠
116942530:
Zlatomesto

Zlatomesto is a small town in Irriseni province of Wintercrux. It is located at the southern part of the province and serves as the shipping center for the ice diamonds mined at Hope Lost and the products of the mines and stone quarries of Skala Foothills. As of 4713 AR, Baroness Sabina Kseniya and her five sullen offspring ruled the town with iron efficiency. Zlatomesto's peasants worked hard, day and night under the lash like slaves, to load the caravans' wagons and sledges.⁠

The Tin King Alley Tavern was the preferred place for the work gangs' masters. The tavern was famous for the potato vodka that it served, but its owner Liisu Nyetesky was a secret agent of the underground movement called the Heralds of Summer's Return, who valued the information she gathered from the drunken patrons concerning the schedule of the most important shipments headed east as it set up ambushes.⁠
125670380:
Ironworks

The Ironworks is one of the largest buildings in Old Korvosa and indeed the entire city. The Ironworks gets pig iron from Janderhoff and recycled slag from local sources and churns out wrought iron of a variety of qualities. Much more a factory than a conventional smithy, the Ironworks focuses on quantity over quality and so never clashes with the city's more quality-focused blacksmiths.⁠

Many of the employees at the Ironworks are also members of the secret guild called the Ironsoots.⁠
127675560:
House of Ensland

The House of Ensland is one of the two most notorious ruins of noble houses and estates in the blasted wasteland of the Furrows, along with Candlehalls.⁠

The house is located four leagues from the ruins of the village of Feldgrau amidst the vast and blackened trench system called the Dead Man's Maze. The estate is almost certainly haunted, as ghost lights are seen playing around the grounds and other-worldly gamblers frequent these noble houses trying to entrap wanderers across the charred lands.⁠

One unsuspecting gambler was Lecit Ghazts, a greedy knight officer who gambled away his body to a devil in the House of Ensland. Ghazts' head still rolls around the Furrows looking for his, or someone else's, body.⁠
136238490:
Droskar's Crucible

Sleeping in the southern shadow of Droskar's Crag⁠ on the edge of Darkmoon Vale lies the now-ruined monastery once known as Droskar's Crucible. At its prime, the monastery was home to dwarven clerics of the malevolent god Droskar, who urged them to ever toil in making weapons on their great forges. The evil forge spurned which came as a result of their worship eventually drove the dwarves out of their haven, and left behind a now-haunted shell of a building. After its fall to decadence and decay, legends began to spread among the dwarves telling of vast riches now lost beneath the crumbling citadel. The greatest dwarven hero, Druingar the Glintaxe, ventured into the depths below the once-sacred site in search of secrets and the ancestral gauntlet the Grasp of Droskar, but he was never heard from again, and inhabitants of the Vale still talk of his ghost haunting the ancient ruins. In the dungeons beneath, the Truescale Kobolds now make their home, ever balanced between their desire to delve deeper into the earth and their fear of what frightening beings lie in wait for them there.⁠
136691500:
Fort Benbem

Fort Benbem is a small port fortress on the Pangalley Atoll in the Shackles. It has been the home port of the Screaming Reaver since the ship was banned from using even Shark Island ports. Black-Eye Benbem had the fortress built using slaves that he drowned soon after its completion. Fort Benbem consists of no more than a dozen wooden buildings surrounded by a log palisade, and is hidden by thick palm trees.⁠

Flickering Tower

The Flickering Tower is the residence of a wizard who has never been seen in the city. Its previous owners sold it in 4645 AR, but although they were compensated for the sale, they don't remember to whom they sold it. Strange lights are seen inside, and opaque windows block the sunlight and view of the interior.⁠ The tower sometimes disappears for months or years, returning either newer or older than before, and those who have sought to uncover its mysteries and enter are later found in the markets, either older or younger, with no memory of their attempts to enter the tower.⁠
168594340:
The Ramps

The Ramps are a series of timber and stone blocks that connect the Inner City and the Lower City. They start at the gates and are designed to collapse in the event of a siege. The ramps are 50 feet wide, and both sides have safety rails to prevent falls, although three or four people die each year from falls here; whether these are accidents or something else is unknown. Various illicit activities take place in the shadow of the ramps, and many criminals take refuge here in search of new victims to rob.⁠
169428710:
Mount Veshka

The summit of Mount Veshka is the tallest point in Brevoy, and the city of Eagle's Watch is located near its summit. It is the sole mountain in the Uvall Hills that span from the Golushkin Mountains in the west to the Icerime Peaks in the east.⁠⁠

Alabastrine

Alabastrine is a city in Druma built in 4607 AR to accommodate Arodenite refugees after the deity's death. However, the migration never happened in the numbers its investors expected, and its hasty construction ceased before it was completed.⁠ High Prophet Kelldor purchased the partially finished city in 4711 AR, and since then the Druman government has auctioned control of the city's districts in five-year spans to the highest bidders.⁠ The most recent auction on record occurred in 4716 AR.
184120700:
Temple of Lost Coins

The Temple of Lost Coins is a half-ruined former church of Trudd⁠ located in the Coins district of Absalom. It is the base of operations of the Forthright, the thieves' guild of the Coins. It is also the residence of the guild master known as the Harlequin.⁠⁠
199623050:
The Pit

The Pit is a forgotten complex from Thassilon used as a research base by Karzoug agents to spy on their enemies Sorshen and especially Alaznist. It was built at a point where the energies of the Outer Rifts were strongest, though the researchers didn't know why.⁠

212154210:
Sothis

The Osirian capital city of Sothis is located just south of the River Sphinx delta, and is the largest, and most prosperous city in the kingdom of Osirion. The city is built around the molted husk of Ulunat, a colossal beetle that was one of the spawn of Rovagug and slain by Ancient Osirion's first pharaoh, Azghaad. Except for a short time under the Four Pharaohs of Ascension, it was also the Osirian capital city before the millennia of Keleshite rule.⁠⁠⁠⁠
218161030:
Twingate

The city of Twingate is located in the north of the nation of Druma on the Gulf of Accord. It is a semipermanent city of tents where the curious come to be initiated into the mysteries of the Prophecies of Kalistrade.⁠
241133560:
Zhobl

Zhobl is a volcano located in the eastern Zho Mountains of Qadira. The eruptions of Zhobl and its companion Zhonar covered the nearby town of Shadun in ash and dust, forcing its inhabitants to abandon it.⁠
273992410:
Charred Meats

The Charred Meats is a butcher shop located on the edge of Dog Town, selling scraps of meat from other butcher shops, which the owner, Chargut, sells to fishermen and farmers. The establishment's secret business is selling corpses, with humanoids fetching the most money, and several disguised undead guard the shop at all times.⁠
274626390:
Viperwall

Viperwall is a notorious keep built on the eastern shores of Ember Lake in central Varisia.⁠ Its many conical towers and serpent carvings emit a sickening green light and poisonous fumes, so it is to no surprise that the place is greatly avoided by the local population.⁠⁠⁠

Rumors suggest that the castle was built in the mid-fifth millennium AR by serpentfolk who traveled up from Sekamina through the Mobhad Leigh in order to create a surface outpost for their people. Others believe that the fortress has existed since the time of Thassilon.⁠ Deep within the keep is a portal to the ruins of Sverenagati.⁠
281095830:
Mivon

The city of Mivon is the capital of the kingdom of Mivon, the only large settlement in the area and the seat of government. It is a walled city built at the confluence of two major rivers: one reaching to Restov (the Shrike River⁠) and the other to New Stetven. Its stone walls have protected the city from a number of sieges, but their foundations constantly sink into the marsh that surrounds the city. The walls also contain granaries and livestock pens.⁠

The great Council Hall stands in the center of the town, and is itself surrounded by stronger walls. The market square surrounds the Council Hall. Most of the buildings are made of wood and are no more than two stories high. Most visitors that are just passing through, stay in the ramshackle huts of the lower quarter. Half the houses here are brothels, gambling dens, drug parlors, and worse. Three different local gangs, the Fast Fallen, the River's Edge Cutters, and the Half-Deads fight for control over the quarter.⁠

The main square of the city of Mivon hosts a weekly gathering, called the Sevier, for swordsmen aged 16 to 60 who wish to duel in public and improve their reputation.⁠⁠

The nine great Aldori Houses and their holdings create a wide ring around the city. Each of the larger families has constructed its own keep of stone or wood on the hills.⁠

The city has a large fishing industry that specialises in catching eels in the pools surrounding the city. It is said that many of the eels have tasted human flesh due to the violent nature of the city, and the phrase "a walk to the fishponds" has a very sinister meaning as the person normally does not return.⁠
289416120:
Scrag Deep

Scrag Deep is an extensive underwater system of caverns at the deepest point of the Glacier Lake in Irrisen.⁠

In the Winter War a tribe of scrags under the command of the great warlord Tirchagac, fought the longships of the Djurstor Confederacy on Glacier Lake. As a reward, Baba Yaga gave the scrags dominion over the Scrag Deep. Scrag Deep is still home of the Scrag Deep tribe descendants of the allies of Baba Yaga.⁠
292803250:
Sunken City

Sunken City is a Thassilonian ruin under the waves in the Howling Straits in the northern reaches of Broken Bay. Known as Udeomel to historians, the sunken city would have been a northerly settlement of Cyrusian.⁠⁠⁠
299380790:
Arkona Palace

Arkona Palace, or Palace Arkona, is a massive black manor atop the highest point of Endrin Isle⁠ that as of 4708 AR housed Old Korvosa's ruling family, House Arkona. Surrounded by an iron-wrought and black-marbled wall, the manor is adorned with strange ornamentation hailing from Vudra, such as doors bearing depictions of Chamidu and decor of elephants with three heads, peacocks holding sabers, and tigers with carved eyes that leer from the palace's walls and over the gardens of the mansion. Ruthless guards patrol the palace.⁠⁠

Beneath Arkona Palace is a famous cyst drop, an occurrence when a sea cave collapses in on itself to form a sinkhole. The cyst drop is formed from the natural caves that compose the Vaults of Korvosa.⁠ The palace's underground levels also include the Vivified Labyrinth, a sprawling and complex obstacle course and dungeon.⁠
306899220:
Sunbleached Tower

The Sunbleached Tower is a bizarre location north of the Qadiran city of Dimayen. It is a massive edifice over 300 feet tall made of interlocking human bones that seems to attract daemons.⁠
310734170:
Bargecrew's Guild Headquarters

The Bargecrew's Guild Headquarters is among Jawbone's fancy businesses, drawing attention for being a bare, undecorated building. The guild members have no interest in participating in local entertainment; their job is to guide people who are using the city's canals and are interested in what the city can offer them.⁠

316474560:
Nexian Embassy

The Nexian Embassy in the city of Katapesh is located in the Inner City district. Katapesh and Nex are natural allies, sharing similar views and business models. The embassy has been built after the dominant architectural style in the city of Quantium. A number of domed buildings topped by narrow spires surround a central courtyard where shrines to the gods form a central ring. Nexian flags cap the spires. The Nexian ambassador in Katapesh is Narlaguut Haraxis. He and his slaves and advisors reside in the embassy. The ambassador spends much of his time in court at the walled Palace of the Pactmasters maintaining goodwill between his country and Katapesh. He spends most of his spare time in Zandrek's Pesh Palace and the Golden Scarab.⁠
325460150:
Menhu Leng

Menhu Leng, also known as Menhu Suu, is a ruined city high in the northern Wall of Heaven mountains of Tian Xia. Menhu Leng sits in the central portion of the mountain range, an area that is known for its links to the nightmare plane of Leng. The cause of this link is much speculated upon, some believe this is due to the height of the mountains tearing at the very fabric of reality itself, while others speculate that in the most distant reaches of the past the denizens of Leng worked to create a primal link with the mountains. Whatever the case, the denizens of Leng now rule over the basalt ruins of Menhu Leng, using their winged shantaks to visit across the lands of Tian Xia to further their sinister schemes.⁠
349604970:
Mount Tsukiyo

Mount Tsukiyo is the tallest mountain in Zi Ha and one of the tallest on the continent of Tian Xia. Located in the Kelsang Mountains and named for the moon deity Tsukiyo, it attracts pilgrims who travel the month-long Tsukiyo Trek in pursuit of guidance from the sky dragon Shei Long, as well as adventure-seeking mountain climbers who race to its summit during the When Earth Touches the Sky Festival.⁠⁠
358422690:
Dusk Market

The Dusk Market is a wandering bazaar that sets up within the shells of fallen temples, theaters, and other opulent ruins within the Westcrown district of Rego Cader. Here the brave and foolish buy contraband, under the very eyes of bribed rundottari (local watch). Drugs, exotic poisons, strange beasts, and kidnapped slaves can all be found in this semi-secret marketplace.⁠⁠⁠

Run by a secret syndicate, it takes place at a different ruin each day in the two hours before sundown—hence its name—to avoid Order of the Rack Hellknights and the city's dangerous creatures.⁠⁠ For a price, almost any local ne'er-do-well can tell visitors where the market will set up next.⁠
365039360:
Monument Circle

Monument Circle, or Fountain Circle, is the name given to a circle of wells and water pumps near Breachill Town Hall in the Isgeri town that locals can use to draw water from the Breach Creek. At its center stands the town's most famous monument: a bronze statue of Lamond Breachton, the founder of Breachill.⁠⁠
368135340:
Iron Harbor

Iron Harbor is a small harbor village on the southern coast of Chakikoth Isle in the Ironbound Archipelago. The ruins of Rusthenge are located on the nearby Thunderhead Isle, which is connected to the village by land during low tide.⁠ Other notable locations include the Gorumite temple called Stonehome; the drydock; Elsie's, an alchemist's shop; and three abandoned manor houses to the west known colloquially as Gold's Ruin.

The village has a single slip shipyard and the aforementioned drydock with nearby workshops to support its activities. The majority of the buildings are single-story stone structures with wood-shingled roofs that consist of simple homes, workshops, general stores, and smoking houses that support the town's fishing industry.⁠

Technically a holding of Xin-Edasseril since the latter's reappearance and conquest of the southern half of the Ironbound archipelago, the village had, until 4723 AR, been mostly left alone, with only the yearly advent of a tax-collector from Xin-Edasseril being the only sign of New Thassilon's newfound control.⁠ Despite these taxes being light, the villagers still rankle at having to pay taxes to anyone, yet they, like the rest of the Kindred Coast, know better than to disturb the status quo.⁠
369587720:
Swiftrun

Swiftrun is a village of superstitious people in Isger, located on the Conerica River about 50 miles from Saringallow.⁠
418717160:
Alabaster Academy

The Alabaster Academy is a widely renowned university in Kintargo's Villegre district, though most of its prestige lies in its past. The academy's reputation was ruined in 4599 AR when a professor was revealed to be a murderer known as the Temple Hill Slasher, and the Chelaxian Civil War ensured it never fully recovered.⁠⁠

The university's focuses include the sciences of botany, medicine, and zoology; practical training in apothecary and healing; and, as a recent addition, arcane magic untainted by Chelaxian requests to incorporate diabolism.⁠⁠

Since at least 4715 AR and as of 4724 AR, the university's headmaster was Iylvana Desdoros.⁠⁠
423082210:
Aerie

The Aerie is a fortress of Andoren Eagle Knights located in the northern reaches of the Kortos Mounts on the Isle of Kortos. Knights assigned to the post deal with thin air due to its elevation, poor food, and local hostilities in order to monitor and prevent any potential threats to Andoran that might originate from the Isle.⁠

As of 4720 AR, several scouts of the Aerie had recently been found decapitated. Despite a lack of evidence suggesting a suspect, most of the fort's troops believed the nearby Gorebreather tribe of minotaurs were responsible.⁠

Redburrow

Redburrow was a mining hamlet in the Hollow Hills specializing in iron ore mining. Several mine shafts surrounded the settlement, providing some defense against attacks, but in 4717 AR the Ironfang Legion overwhelmed the defenders, burning the houses and its inhabitants to the ground.⁠
474980790:
Toduc Wa

Toduc Wa (pronounced tu-duk wah)⁠ was once the largest city in the Tian Xia nation of Linvarre, which was formerly the Taldan colony of Amanandar. The Monastery of the Blended Forms, a renowned martial arts retreat inspired by Taldor's Tian-founded Monastery of the Seven Forms, is located in Toduc Wa.⁠
477687040:
Broadfoot Marshals Station House

Broadfoot Marshals Station House is a base for a private firefighting brigade in The Docks district of Absalom. Under the instruction of the dwarven engineer Bagara Broadfoot, they use water carts that, through pedals, can create pressure to expel water and extinguish fires, which are quite dangerous in a district made almost entirely out of wood.⁠

490370580:
Dreamer's Reach

The barren peak of Dreamer's Reach is also one of the highest in the area. It holds special significance for the Kellid people, who often seek divine guidance at this site. They undergo a spiritual journey to the mountain's summit, where they remove all of their clothes above the waist and wait in the harsh cold conditions for a waking dream from Desna. Barring that, they continue waiting until spirits take them away to the Boneyard.⁠⁠

Despite its spiritual importance, Dreamer's Reach is a place rarely visited by animals and giants, thus, the physical challenges and exposure to the elements most threaten those who make the treacherous climb. However, this location is also a place where the boundary between the Universe and the Dreamlands is thin, and people who seek visions at Dreamer's Reach might find themselves engaged in fierce battles with nightmares that become dangerously real.⁠
496005370:
Ghataking

Located in the central Napsune Mountains of Rahadoum, the mountain Ghataking is most famous for the foul inhabitants who dwell upon it. Ghataking is the lair of a zahhak, a powerful type of azi dragon, named Khanjar-Khanayr but more commonly known as "Stone Maw". He lairs on this peak awaiting a divine prophecy delivered by foul Ahriman himself and is served by a cult of Usij, evil div-worshippers all but wiped out by the church of Sarenrae.⁠
496150210:
Langkhu

Langkhu is a city of inland Goka, near a gap in the Wall of Heaven in western Tian Xia.⁠⁠
498597370:
Grotto of St. Elth

The Grotto of St. Elth is a small shrine dedicated to Sarenrae in a grove near the Arthfell Forest. The body of Elth Hammerson is buried in the grotto, which was made a holy site by the High Priest of Sarenrae in Almas after his sacrifice saving lives. Once a year, on the anniversary of his death, he manifests and those who have visited him notice that he appears increasingly melancholic.⁠
509283360:
Rachikan

The ruins of the ancient Jistkan city of Rachikan were discovered in 4709 AR by the Pathfinder Eldis Grone among the Pillars of Anferita in southwestern Cheliax.⁠⁠

It is the site of a Grand Athenaeum expedition led by Marianix Karn.⁠⁠
511541030:
Solanas

Solanas is a frontier town in the region of the River Kingdoms controlled by Daggermark.

As of 4710 AR it was ruled by the Solanas Concern criminal gang, and while the town's sheriff does what he can to keep the peace, the Concern interferes to protect its interests. Solanas' people are accustomed to daily killings and assassinations that happen every day, and the mayor had sent an emissary to Daggermark to beg lord Martro Livondar for help.

Solanas is home to an important Pathfinder lodge, complete with a main hall, a dormitory, and a stable full of fresh horses. The lodge is guarded by a group of mercenaries.⁠
521397680:
House of the Senses Awakened

The House of the Senses Awakened was the decadent project of Grand Prince Cydonus III, the ruler of Taldor who was so profligate in his spending that, during a mere five-year reign (4077–4081 AR), he nearly bankrupted the entire country. Cydonus spent his life wracked with anxiety over the possibility of an attack from neighbouring Qadira. He dealt with this fear by indulging his every whim and the culmination of this was the House of the Senses Awakened. A maze-like pleasure palace located in the wilds of the Porthmos Gap, Cydonus III effectively moved Taldor's capital from Oppara to this lavish pleasure ground during his reign. This included his harem of lovers and one in particular, Origen Sarlu, was especially fond of the Grand Prince.⁠

In the wake of the Even-Tongued Conquest, Grand Prince Cydonus III was poisoned by a Qadiran agent (later identified by the Ballingar Accord).⁠ After the Grand Prince's death, Origen Sarlu absconded with his body and sealed himself, the Grand Prince's body, and a significant portion of Taldor's wealth within the House of the Senses Awakened, turning the complex into a trap-riddled hazard that has remained impenetrable to this day. Origen Sarlu still dwells within, having become a powerful form of undead known as a nemhain. The house is also protected by an array of other undead, including spectres, wights, and wraiths, as well as ancient stone golems.⁠
522553030:
Raven's Watch

Raven's Watch was a fort constructed on the northern banks of the Turandarok River in the Ravenroost tors of Varisia's Sandpoint Hinterlands. The prison was abandoned when Sandpoint grew large enough to support its own garrison and jail, and rumours about a haunting or a curse have swirled around the prison since.

Though the above-ground portion of the prison quickly crumbled into ruin, the lower portions, where the guards were said to have left some prisoners, remain largely intact. A band of bandits aligned with the cult of Lamashtu are now said to have taken up watch within the prison's ruins.⁠
550932150:
Stormspear Keep

The Stormspear Keep of the Blackravens is located at the northeastern corner of the region of Hagreach in the Lands of the Linnorm Kings. It is a complex of towers perched upon a cliff nearly 2,000 feet high at the northernmost edge of the border between Hagreach and Irrisen. The Blackraven warriors are allied with many nests of giant eagles, who help them patrol the northern borders.⁠
553640980:
Yuming

Yuming is a massive city located in the former heartland of Imperial Lung Wa in the Successor State of Po Li. The nation is ruled by the powerful Oracular Council that allows no worship of other deities other than that of the idea of the Eternal Emperor.⁠
557868430:
Drowning Rock

Drowning Rock is a small town on the southwestern side of the island of Tempest Cay in the Shackles. Its position largely shields it from the stormy winds of the north.

The town is built around a towering monolith that gradually sinks into the muddy soil, and the townsfolk hold their landmark in high esteem. Every summer the town throws a two-day festival, and the main event involves the strongest men coming together and hoisting the rock from the muck via rope and pulley. The town economy is based on its farms and clam fields.⁠
573132170:
Losthome

Losthome is an Ulfen logging town in the far east of the Grungir Forest in the Lands of the Linnorm Kings. Located on the banks of the Thundering River, though not actually within the Linnorm Kingdom of the Thanelands, Losthome is protected by Kalsgard. Its people, many of them descendants of refugees from the Winter War, constantly watch the border with Irrisen for signs of incursion, and provide sanctuary to anyone fleeing the realm of the Witch Queen.⁠⁠⁠
578102560:
House of Yanti Purnállo

The House of Yanti Purnállo is the home of the last remaining hero-god of Xopatl, Purnállo. While most of the hero-gods are mythic figures of ancient history who have long since ascended to true godhood, disappeared, or died, Purnállo chose a different path. Thousands of years ago, Purnállo undertook a unique process: she began to meditate while ritually wrapping herself in the enhanced vines and leaves of Xopatl's plant life, eventually effectively mummifying herself while still alive. This mummification resulted in Purnállo reducing even her essential life processes to an almost imperceptibly slow speed. Over the centuries the people of Xopatl erected a temple around the remains of Purnállo and now the people flock in pilgrimage to the House of Yanti Purnállo to hear the saint's heart beat once per century.⁠
598446610:
Yargos's Mission

Yargos's Mission is the most reliable charitable organization in The Puddles, where Yargos Gill, the old veteran, puts a portion of his fortune to provide food and medicine to the most unfortunate in the district. Unfortunately, that includes basically the entire district, and the workers have their hands full running the charity while also having to watch out for the most nefarious elements who seek to get their hands on their resources.⁠

Zimar

One of the main defensive Taldan strongholds against any future invasion from the south, Zimar is vital to the long term survival of the nation. Even though Taldor has not been openly at war with its southern neighbor since 4079 AR, the city remains ever watchful and is the most heavily fortified settlement in Taldor.⁠⁠

Ashpeak

The Ashpeak is a dormant volcano in the Mindspin Mountains, where clans of fire giants have resided for generations. The volcano rises approximately 7,000 feet and boasts large forests at its base. Numerous tunnels have been renovated by the giants, serving as fortresses. They have created openings that allow rainwater to pass through, and various signs have been placed to guide them through the labyrinthine tunnels.⁠

Aeldervenk Manor

Aeldervenk Manor, located in The Greens district of Kintargo, Ravounel, is the home of the Aeldervenk family.⁠ As of 4715 AR, this minor aristocratic family was not considered to be among one of Kintargo's great noble houses.⁠

Shrine of Shelyn

The priests listen to the woes of artists and offer counsel to couples, and the shrine is frequented by many of the district's performers.⁠

Heskott Bay

Heskott Bay was a town founded on the cursed island of Whyrlis Rock in the Shackles. It was located on one of the three decent anchorages left on the island. It was built as an outpost for the fleet of the pirate lord Baillie Heskott in the early years of the Shackles. It seems that three years after its foundation, all the residents of the town vanished into thin air. Those few who visited the abandoned town said that they heard the sounds of a busy city interrupted by screams of terror.⁠
649429980:
Church of Asmodeus

The Church of Asmodeus is one of the youngest building of the Ascendant Court, the religious heart of Absalom, with the previous high temple to Asmodeus having been burned to the ground during the so-called "Devil's Night Uprising" in 4698 AR. Instead of rebuilding on the old grounds, the new Church of Asmodeus was built, it was completed in 4705 AR, just months before the centenary anniversary of the death of Aroden. While Infernal Cheliax is the home of Asmodeus's worship in the Inner Sea region, the Church of Asmodeus in Absalom serves as a home for those outside of Cheliax. Worshippers at the Church of Asmodeus include ancestries that normally face prejudice and persecution within Cheliax, such as tieflings, halflings and even the rare strix. This acceptance puts the Church somewhat at odds with Cheliax and the nearby Chelaxian embassy.⁠ In particular, the high priestess of the Church of Asmodeus, the so-called "Beloved of Asmodeus", Scion Lady Xansippe of House Tevineg is caught between her unwavering devotion to the faith of Asmodeus and her duty to both her ancestral homeland of Cheliax⁠ and her husband Lord Gulv of House Tevineg, the recently appointed grand ambassador of Cheliax.⁠
664557480:
Rookwarden

Located in the Loric Fells, Rookwarden is a stone and granite fortress built by dwarves in 4636 AR. Situated on the bluff of a quarry rich with marble, this fortress is easily defended by even a small number of soldiers. According to rumor, a secret network of tunnels honeycombs beneath the fortress and allegedly leads to entrances that could be used to take the fortress without an extended siege.

The history of the fortress is closely tied with the history of Loric Fells, with a rich history of occupation, from dwarves to humans to goblins and trolls.⁠
666029240:
Golushkin

Golushkin is a dwarven settlement located in the Golushkin Mountains. The Golka clan leads the settlement. These dwarves had a trade relationship with House Garess of Brevoy, but all contact has been lost from roughly the same time as the Vanishing of Brevoy's House Rogarvia.⁠
678901480:
Lyceum

The Lyceum is a college for bards and entertainers that produces the finest in Varisia, though Magnimar and Korvosa never acknowledge this. The college's egalitarian policy was established by its founder, Tharius Giovée, and his great-grandson, Thaddeus Giovée, continues the practice. The college houses the largest altar to Shelyn in the city and is a popular meeting place for lovers.⁠
679489700:
Imnuxeos

Imnuxeos is an ancient, haunted remainder of the long-collapsed Ghol-Gan empire. Located south of the Terwa Uplands and north of Bloodcove, Imnuxeos is now little more than a stretch of isolated badlands dotted with remnants of colossal masonry from 10,000 years ago.⁠

At the height of the Ghol-Gan civilisation, Imnuxeos was the most brutal fighting pit in the kingdom, a colossal coliseum where cyclops gladiators faced off against captured monsters, slaves, or even other cyclopes in bloodbaths of exceptional spectacle. The ghosts of these ancient gladiators still linger, and every night as darkness falls Imnuxeos's champions rise once more to face each other—and any mortal foolish enough to remain. Those who linger after sunset face undead cyclopes, horrific aberrations, and reanimated beasts of ancient bone.⁠
690516970:
Gladiators' Guildhall

The Gladiators' Guildhall is a structure of bone and hide where the city's gladiators train with strange weapons and in unique styles, practicing day and night. Battles are held constantly, with fierce stakes and high mortality rates.⁠
691393230:
Silk Castle

The Silk Castle is a kite shop located in the Wise Quarter of Absalom. Its proprietor, Vittar Corusec, is often hired to judge special kite-fighting battles in the Irorium during the Gala of Sails and Kraken Carnival festivals held in spring and autumn respectively.⁠
706069470:
Canaroden

Canaroden is the longest and deepest canal in Westcrown, physically separating Parego Spera and Parego Dospera. The canal walls in the southern area feature bas-reliefs of the city's founders, while those in the north depict faces of Aroden. Thanks to the magical properties of these walls, they have remained undisturbed for centuries after their construction. In the past, eight bridges spanned the canal, though only two remain: Bladewing Bridge and Truemount Bridge.⁠
725264920:
Merry Pranksters

The Merry Pranksters is a group of two dozen pirates who survive on the island of Hesmene's Grotto in the Shackles.⁠
727360950:
Flesk

Flesk is a settlement on the central eastern coast of the Isle of Kortos in the nation of Absalom.⁠
728238900:
Kirya

The temple city of Kirya is located in the peaks above the Syrzemyan Highlands of Iobaria, and is accessible only by flight or via the cyclopean Koloran road that runs across the Grenalthrost and the Grenalf Plateau. An ancient cyclops temple city surrounding a clear mountain lake called Orost-Kar, the modern city of Kirya was founded by the Ulfen explorer Grenalf in 846 AR who named the city after his wife. Priests of various Iobarian faiths soon reconsecrated the temples to their own gods, and the city became a centre for pilgrimages from across Iobaria.⁠

Kirya eventually became one of Iobaria's largest cities, with new building materials brought in from the Orostgard forest, until the logging awoke something, leading to the depopulation of Kirya by 1574 AR. Since then, various powers have taken control of Kirya, including a group of cyclopes and hill giants who built the Temples of Blood and Bone out of human bodies. The cyclopes and giants were cleared out by one of Iobaria's many plagues, and succeeded by hobgoblins, who ruled until the rise of New Iobaria in 3212 AR when humans reclaimed Kirya.⁠

Under the leadership of grand druid Fedor Vasylk, the temple city is maintaining its independence in the conflicts between Orlov, Kridorn, and Mirnbay. Its inhabitants embrace 36 local nature gods who are seen as Erastil's children.⁠

Dragons who were once allies of Iobaria's noble houses are known to inhabit the ruins beneath Kirya.⁠

Delronge Estate, located in The Greens district of Kintargo, Ravounel, is the home of House Delronge.⁠⁠
737870700:

Tripolne is the seat of the Backar territory of Molthune.⁠
756720910:
Bastion of the Nail

In Magnimar, the Hellknight Order of the Nail is headquartered within the Bastion of the Nail in the Naos district. The Order was invited to Magnimar by a portion of the Justice Court. Darean Halst leads this contingent, which also takes private commissions from groups or individuals needing great protection.⁠
765193300:
Valley of the Chosen Children

The Valley of the Chosen Children is a canyon of the Naurepzi River in Xopatl after it flows away from the Follower's River.⁠ Locals claim that at night the laughter of dozens of children echoes through the valley, and that anyone who sails the entire length of the Valley of the Chosen Children in a single night receives some kind of blessing.⁠
766202020:
Palace of Thirteen Spires

The Palace of Thirteen Spires is a small but opulent palace in the Wise Quarter, divided into four wings, each in a Chelaxian, Osirian, Taldan, and Minkan style. For most of the year, the rooms are rented to merchants and nobles visiting the city.⁠ The White Grotto holds the contract to the estate, working with the Wise Council to manage the building exclusively, a fact that greatly displeases the Arcanamirium. When a head of state visits, everyone else is evicted so the best rooms can be reserved for royalty, and the money raised goes toward public works and scholarships.⁠
772316360:
Edme

The city of Edme, in the easternmost reaches of Galt north of the Boarwood, was once a great center of learning.⁠
777200190:
Oakrib Inn

Oakrib Inn is the site where the Silver Ravens negotiated the details of Ravounel's secession from Cheliax. This large inn near the head of the Yolubilis River was once a popular stopping point for those traveling through the Menador Gap. Since the destruction of Menador Keep and the closure of the Gap, the inn's owner Olradi Ormovor⁠ has reinvented it as a luxury tourist destination and historical heritage site, complete with dramatic reenactments of the tense negotiations.⁠

The south wing houses the laboratories where dozens of alchemists work and where Yamthar keeps his collection of Jistkan artifacts, which he has acquired and attempts to reactivate, including those that are normally dormant.⁠
783579510:
Kragnaroth

The fire giant kingdom of Kragnaroth is located in the Mindspin Mountains, east of Varisia. Its current ruler is King Orynox Marchelin, a fierce and ruthless warlord who has plans to expand Kragnaroth across the Mindspin Mountains both south and east. Orynox's latest queen is Hregana and he seems to be especially preoccupied by her.⁠ He has been married to her longer than his previous five wives combined.⁠⁠

Outsiders would be very confused by the giants referring to this place as a "kingdom", as it is not much bigger than a large city that spans about 15 square miles.⁠ It consists of three towers arranged around a valley that house about 250 fire giants, with hundreds of smaller humanoid slaves who serve as farmers and in forges.⁠

Bellezeph Villa

Haven

Haven is a secluded and tranquil village nestled within a hidden valley to the north of Hillcross in the Tusk Mountains. Tanglegate

Treerazer, the lord of Tanglebriar, hopes one day to be able to use Tanglegate against the elves, and so he has ordered his minions to refrain from destroying it. The gate itself is a stone arch covered in moss, and it stands on a rare patch of dry ground in the middle of a stinking bog. ⁠

Solskinn

Solskinn is a small town in the Linnorm Kingdom of Southmoor, located to the south of Grungir Forest and to the north-east of Southmoor's capital of Jol.

As of 4711 AR it was officially ruled by Southmoor's Linnorm King Opir Eightfingers, but local leaders would take control whenever they felt that they could. Pleasant during the day, the small town was under forced curfew at night, as anyone leaving their homes is abducted by the visiting shadows.⁠

Ashkurhall

Ashkurhall is an ancient abandoned dwarven settlement in Mount Nakyuk, located in a jungle vale of the Mwangi Expanse known by as the Valley of Broken Blood. It was the subject of the final expedition by the Pathfinder Society Venture-Captain Nieford Sharrowsmith, which led to his death.⁠⁠
848392440:
Kamawgyar Shrine

The abandoned Kamawgyar Shrine is located in the Zho Mountains of Qadira northeast of the Pashman River. It features a massive statue of the god Irori placed over a natural cave where the priests who once served the shrine lived. It is now the home of a mother and daughter harpy who were exiled from the large harpy community at Al-Bashir, along with a small retinue of dire corbies.⁠
851613650:
Hero's Rest

Hero's Rest, in the Hagreach region of the Lands of the Linnorm Kings, is a memorial to honor the most famous of those who have died defending Hagreach from the Irriseni raiders and whose bodies have not been recovered, remaining where they were slain across the border in Irrisen. All Hero's Rest cairns and graves are empty and the memorial is also known as the Empty Boneyard. The hilltop memorial which overlooks the eastern border is protected by a silver dragon named Avaleru. The dragon has no true love for the violent Ulfen neighbors, but she hates the Irriseni witches and their agents. It is said that Avaleru uses a part of the regular yearly tithes she gets as a guardian to grant magical boons to kind and good-mannerly Ulfen, assuming the form of a mysterious silver-haired woman.⁠

The hill of Hero's Rest is located on the western bank of the Iceflow River, 50 miles north of Blackraven Hall and opposite τhe Irriseni towns of Yensa and Soduras.⁠⁠
853586930:
Dockside Giant

The Dockside Giant is a massive copper statue located in Katapesh's Docks district that depicts a bearded man with horns and a large trident staring menacingly out to sea. The statue has been there since at least 2589 AR and is seen by the locals as a ward against bad weather and bad luck. The locals must constantly battle against the elements to keep the statue clean and decent.

There are various theories as to who or what the statue depicts. Some believe it depicts an ancient hero, while others believe it is a now-dead deity of the sea. Whatever it depicts, the Dockside Giant has become a landmark of the Docks.⁠
854487460:
Everlasting Palace

The Everlasting Palace is a magnificent structure of white marble and golden domes where High Prophet Kelldor directs the affairs of the Kalistocracy, surrounded by guards from the Mercenary League who protect him and a host of constructs powered by the souls of those who have fallen in his defense. In the upper dome are dozens of mirrors with which Kelldor can communicate with the leaders of the various nations of Golarion to maintain Druma's trade dominance.⁠
861421080:
Dbede

The tower of Dbede is 100 feet tall and 50 feet wide and was built by termites. It dominates the skyline near the center of the Screaming Jungle in the southern Mwangi Expanse, and early explorers mistakenly assumed it marked the site of an ancient lost city. Millions of termites inhabit the tower, and they fiercely defend their home against any trespassers, as is evidenced by the thousands of clean-picked skeletons that litter the ground around it. The Screaming Jungle's intelligent inhabitants occasionally use the termites' ferocity to execute captives in a truly gruesome manner. Hundreds of similar termite mounds can be found on the Korir Plains north of the jungle, but none compares in size to Dbede.⁠
861908210:
Baakai

The town of Baakai is the largest human settlement in Shenmen.⁠
872878950:
Obrand's Stand

Obrand's Stand is a fort on the western edge of Corentyn with high walls that provide approximately a mile of space for archers ready to attack invaders. Throughout Corentyn's history, the fort has never been breached by an invader.⁠

Obrand's Stand is one of the nine famous forts of Corentyn, the City of Nine Forts, according to the classical listing.⁠
880065640:
Xefon-Ra

Xefon-Ra is a mountain in the desert of northern Osirion. It is located between the Glazen Sheets and the Sahure Wastes.⁠
880116050:
Vault of the Impostor Goblin

No one is entirely sure what is inside the Vault of the Imposter Goblin. A few even doubt its existence, though it certainly does. The vault has one large stone entryway that connects to a larger underground complex.⁠
900981360:
Celwynvian Charge

The Celwynvian Charge is a stony, tree-shaped monument in Magnimar's Lowcleft district. It grows real leaves that appear and fall in the appropriate seasons. This gift from the elves of the Mierani Forest was in response to a trade delegation from Magnimar proposing an alliance (which never materialized). Local legend says that meditating here improves one's reflexes.⁠

Rising to a height of thirty feet, the monument is made from white wood and crystal. Through a clever trick of natural mathematics, the tree appears symmetrical from every angle, though this natural illusion can be uncovered by a careful observer.⁠

Lod

Lod is a small Irriseni town near the headwaters of the Marbleflow River in Hoarwood province.⁠⁠

Lod is the first stop of the trade path north along the Marbleflow River. The town welcomes Varisian merchants and its river front is full of wharves and warehouses. A dry dock called Cold Queen Waters repairs damaged barges and also crafts and sells small riverboats. Seven inns are close to the docks serving the merchants, riverboat captains, and their crews. The Boar's Head inn is renowned for its attached brothel and gambling house, run by the siblings Grevel and Holz Nabotov. Other known inns in the docks are the Sister Helena's and the Warm Doxy.⁠

The wealthy widowed owner of half a dozen warehouses, Vilma Lochnik is secretly a member of the underground anti-government movement Heralds of Summer's Return. Vilma is efficient in smuggling refugees out of Irrisen.⁠

Baroness Arisa is the ruler of the town of Lod. She has tried to open an overland trade path between Lod and the provincial capital of Hoarwood through the forest but she cannot deal with a strangely well-organized group of bandits called the Bitter Brotherhood.⁠
926395270:
Gralton

The inhabitants of Gralton consist almost entirely of people who have fled the ongoing revolution (some would say anarchy) in Galt. Many of those who have fled to Gralton are the old nobility of Galt. Deposed and fallen from grace, they desperately seek any means to regain what they have lost, be it by sponsoring counter-revolutionary activity, or sending parties of hapless adventurers back into Galt to search for family heirlooms left behind in the rush to escape the guillotine's blade. As the desperation of the deposed nobility grew, Gralton began to attract con-artists and tricksters. These tried to hustle the desperate nobility by offering quick fixes and false hope.⁠ The town has two notable temples: one to the drunken hero deity, Cayden Cailean,⁠ the other to the Vengeful Sting, Calistria. In fact, many suspect the people of Gralton to be possessed by some spirit of Calistria. So bent on vengeance against Galt are they, that many see divine intervention in their hate-filled eyes.⁠

Lantern Lodge

After being purchased by Venture-Captain Amara Li for a large sum of money, the Lantern Lodge in the Petal District⁠ of Absalom reflects the finest culture that the city has to offer. During her many trips to Absalom, she purchased many furnishings for the lodge and has brought them back to Goka, currently on display even today. The lodge is kept extremely clean and Amara Li expects her guests to conduct themselves professionally. Any Pathfinder who is heading on a long journey usually stops by this lodge before leaving.⁠

Barque Bazaar

The Barque Bazaar is a floating business where several barges have joined together, and merchants sell their foreign goods to customers all along the Absalom coast. Created by Market Master Annavi, she believed her business would be a success, but she hadn't anticipated that the residents of The Puddles, The Docks, and Precipice Quarter would be the poorest in the city, and she's struggling to keep the business afloat, both literally and figuratively. 951458880:
Orisini Academy

A famous sword-training school built in the center of the Old Dock ward of the Varisian city of Korvosa's Old Korvosa district, the Orisini Academy, features a grand archway and balcony with ornate oak doors. Located at 16 Hillcrest Street, its door knockers feature the shape of an imp and pseudodragon seemingly locked in lethal combat. Mostly young heirs of noble houses of the city enroll in the academy to learn and practice the art of fencing. The school's namesake, Vencarlo Orisini, rarely teaches the classes himself and leaves the responsibility to one of his senior students named Dengaro, instead.⁠⁠
953748450:
Metringer Sanitarium

Metringer Sanitarium has been in operation since 4000 AR, serving as a place of healing and medicine for those suffering from mental illness, as well as a site for ethically questionable experiments on these patients. Its director, Flevvid Grummlin, has shown the facility to the Sally Guard on several occasions, but they have found nothing out of the ordinary. In secret dungeons, patients deemed unfit for service are taken to end their stay. Salindra Concilio escaped the building and has been warning others and seeking help to reveal the situation inside, though many consider her delusional. Only one person is offering a reward for this information.⁠
956252090:
Korvosa

Korvosa (pronounced kohr-VOH-sah)⁠ is the largest city in Varisia, and was once the capital of Chelaxian Varisia.⁠ It now serves as the seat of one of three city-states that claim independent authority over their individual holdings in the region. Though its citizens and traditions have strong ties to the nation of Cheliax, with many of its people tracing their ancestry directly to servants of the Empire, the city's location at the mouth of the Jeggare River and the presence of a highly-defensible harbor have contributed to the establishment of Korvosa as a primary hub for trade. Various cultures and peoples live within the city's walls as goods move in and out of its gates.⁠

It is currently ruled by Queen Cressida Kroft, who was selected to rule by the city's seneschal upon the death of the city's previous monarch, Queen Ileosa Arabasti.⁠
959666070:
Chimera Cove

Chimera Cove is a small, nominally Andoren fishing village located on Aspo Bay on the northern shores of the Inner Sea.⁠ The coast here is rough, battered by waves and wind, and usually cloaked in fog. The village sprang up during the difficult years following Andoran's split with Cheliax and is named Chimera Cove because of the three large islands just offshore: the Lion, the Dragon, and the Goat.⁠ Due to its precarious location, the town has failed to expand and thrive, although its residents have no trouble feeding themselves via subsistence farming and fishing.⁠
963834450:
Tilxar

Little is known about Tilxar, a location in northeastern Geb near the Ydrion River.⁠

Tower of Winds

The Tower of Winds is a strange structure located on a peninsula on the Plains of Paresh in northwestern Qadira near the Inner Sea's Saray Coast.⁠⁠

Breachill Archives

The Breachill Archives in the Isgeri town is a building that collects and preserves all the town's official documents from its founding to the present day. Librarian Jorell Blacktusk is responsible for keeping the documents in order, and although it is a great responsibility, his interest in Breachill's history is motivation enough. The first pages of the archives were written by the founder, Lamond Breachton, and since then, the townspeople have compiled their experiences for posterity.⁠
969030610:
Shadowreach

Despite its appearance as a rural paradise, locals have shunned the ivy-covered hunting lodge named Shadowreach in Nidal's southern Uskwood for years. The area is infested with lethal shadow creatures, and rumors circulate about even more perilous dangers lurking among the nearby trees.⁠
975556140:
Dead Villages

The Dead Villages are a collection of abandoned villages in the Brazen Frontier section of southern Osirion. They were once inhabited by Pharasmin death cults who believed that one's afterlife could be positively influenced by choosing the time of one's demise. This led the villagers to engage in ritual combat to the death as well as suicide. These practices guaranteed that the cult soon ran out of members, leaving the villages empty.

As of 4714 AR bones could still be found in the central squares of these empty settlements, and distressed undead such as allips haunt them at night. Although the cultists believed they were worshiping Pharasma, its leaders secretly were devotees of Sifkesh, demon lord of heresy and suicide.⁠
994245320:
Bundózo

Bundózo is a town located on the northern bank of the Lake of the Blessed Prince in the central part of Xopatl. Its economy depends on diving expeditions into a massive underwater keep, which was home to a hero-god who chose to submerge it upon his ascension. The fort seems to be dozens of storeys tall, and has yet to be fully scoured of its treasures.⁠
994866470:
Wispil

Located in the depths of the Verduran Forest, Wispil is the gnomish city responsible for most of Taldor's supply of timber and much of its wood craft. Wispil provides the timber that fuels the bustling Imperial Naval Shipyards of Cassomir, which in turn grant the Taldan Imperial Navy its power.⁠
1004481450:
Siphons

The Siphons are a system of underground tunnels beneath the Absalom district of the Puddles. They consist of parts of the city's larger sewer system as well as an intricate series of crypts and emergency tunnels. The frequently flooded nature of these tunnels makes them an ideal location for criminals, who find that the risk of collapse and drowning are enough to keep the law away, and many thieves' guilds and other nefarious elements shore up walls and use the system for their lairs. Perhaps the best-known of the Siphons' residents is the information broker Grandmaster Torch.⁠
1015444340:
Morilla Palace and the Tally Wall

3 locations:
  • Damaq Palace
  • Palace Ormuz
  • Uiry Manor Museum
1018066830:
Iron and Hoof Gate

The Iron and Hoof Gate is the southwestern fortified entrance to the Andoren capital of Almas. It leads directly into the industrial and working class Tamuth District, and is wide enough to accommodate both draft animals and large wagons.⁠
1026421880:
District Courthouse

The District Courthouse of the Ascendant Court is where the district's less serious criminal trials are held, overseen by a trio of elderly judges of Abadar. Their judgments are fair, but the work here is usually quite slow, with a waiting list for filing a complaint or processing a grievance.⁠
1028866590:
Menador Keep

Menador Keep is a two-story dwarven-engineered gatehouse at the narrowest point of the Menador Gap, which connects the Chelaxian Archduchy of Menador to Ravounel through the Menador Mountains. The keep forms a short, artificial tunnel that bottlenecks traffic, which House Thrune staffs with loyal soldiers who exert heavy taxes and strict regulations on travel.⁠

During the Glorious Reclamation insurgency of 4716 AR, Menador Keep was commanded by Lucian Thrune.⁠
1029234240:
Alvis

Located in the Arthfell region of southern Andoran near Aspo Bay, the town of Alvis is best known for a series of kidnappings perpetrated by a local cult in 4708 AR.⁠ Alvis is also home to the Andoran Alchemical Society.⁠

In 4708 AR the Sheriff of Alvis was an idealistic young man named Eraltis.⁠

In 4725 AR many people came to the town to join the guild to investigate the effects of the Godsrain, creating a need for new housing.⁠
1030460750:
Mistshroud Cliff

Mistshroud Cliff is in the eastern reaches of the Eismonts mountain range, south of the Maiestas River in southwestern Cheliax.⁠⁠
1050815110:
Rangdol

Rangdol is a city of scholarship in southern Zi Ha. Its guilds—which include the Engineering & Architecture Guild, Mages Guild, and Scholars Guild—help to develop some of the nation's most prominent intellects, and the city is also renowned for its automated transportation, libraries, and second underground city that accommodates its population during the intense summers.⁠
1057478180:
Emperor's Pass

Emperor's Pass is a mountain pass in the northern edge of the Southern Range mountains of Taldor, directly north of the town of Tribulation.⁠
1074472290:
Well of Gorum

The Well of Gorum was formed when a piece of his armor struck Almas, thankfully only destroying a couple of empty warehouses, and the metal was recovered by the city guard. After the storms, the crater has filled with water, and a patrol anxiously watches the area.⁠
1077050800:
Zincher's Camp

Zincher's Camp is the area designated by Clegg Zincher after he was taken over by the drow, as it was the closest location to the sea caves where they hid. Two hunters' houses are located in the area, though they are in danger of collapse, so no one uses them for shelter.⁠
1082950790:
Silver Star

The Silver Star, once a music store in the foreign quarter of the Jarvis End district of Kintargo, is as of 4724 AR a vacant lot.⁠
1084887290:
Everpine

Everpine is an unusual fey settlement in the western Barrowood of Cheliax.⁠
1085598110:
Gerig's Workshop

Gerig's Workshop is where the popular drink of Gerig the Inspirer is produced, and since its production is a trade secret, there are always many Guild of Spears guards patrolling the area.⁠
1087396290:
Crowhollow

Crowhollow is a sinkhole in the Sellen Hills of northeastern Numeria, and the site of a piece of the Divinity that fell during the Rain of Stars. It is also the home of a half-mechanical lich named Alling Third, a former Technic League agent who sought immortality in order to fully exploit its technology.⁠⁠⁠
1087990540:
Sevenarches

Sevenarches is a town in the southwestern River Kingdoms built around seven stone arches scattered around the settlement, and a loosely organized nation of the surrounding wildlands. It is an ancient site sacred to elves, but has not been in elven hands since they left Golarion for the safety of Sovyrian millennia ago.

Since then, Sevenarches has been under the rule of the Oakstewards, a group of secretive druids. Indeed, Sevenarches is the only surviving kingdom from the initial wave of Kellid migration into the River Kingdoms region after the exit of the elves.⁠⁠
1104881790:
Tsering Springs

The Tsering Springs (pronounced SEAR-ing Springs)⁠ are the ancestral home of the samsarans of Zi Ha in Tian Xia. The settlement allows entry to outsiders only on invitation or when accompanied by a samsaran guide.⁠
1114216540:
Starrise Spire

The Starrise Spire, the tallest building in Nerosyan, is located on the city's outer wall in the Confluence District neighborhood of Coopertown. It is topped by a celestial light that continuously shines in even the darkest of nights and never fades as long as at least one defender still resides in the tower. This beacon provided hope and relief to adventurers that crusaders still stood against the demons of the Worldwound,⁠ and continues to operate as a center of restoration efforts since the Worldwound's closure into the Sarkoris.⁠ Before the Pathfinder Society was tasked to protect the city, the city's crusaders defended its walls.⁠⁠

The Starrise Spire's venture-captain is Jorsal of Lauterbury,⁠⁠ a well-decorated Mwangi man with over 50 advances into the Worldwound under his belt.⁠ Jorsal delegates divine magic training and consecration of the Spire's holy sites to Seeker Ereth Brightmane.⁠
1117257960:
Shadun

The ruins of the Qadiran town of Shadun are located in the eastern foothills of the Zho Mountains, on the opposite side of the mountain range from Gurat. The hillsides around the town were once covered in terrace farms watered by the tributaries of the Pashman River, and criss-crossed with green trails. Tragedy struck when the nearby volcanoes Zhonar and Zhobl began spewing great clouds of dust and ash that covered the countryside, forcing the town's inhabitants to flee. No one is quite sure what happened to the citizens of Shadun, and today its desolate streets are stalked at night by strange shadowy figures with eyes like glowing embers.⁠
1130184230:
Whisper Creek

Whisper Creek is a small settlement halfway between Blackridge and Crackspike in Devil's Perch. It used to be within the Chelaxian Archduchy of Menador⁠ but is now within the nation of Ravounel.⁠
1132120160:
Collapsed Halls

The Collapsed Halls are the haunted ruins of a castle located on the upper Maiestas River west of the Barrowood, near the borders of the Chelaxian Archduchies of Menador and the Heartlands.⁠⁠⁠
1139382000:
Windspire

Windspire is an independent roost of the Windspire tribe of strix in Devil's Perch, within the borders of the Chelaxian Archduchy of Menador.⁠⁠⁠
1143007770:
Badelund

Badelund is a well-fortified town on the Frozen Road, in the north of the Irriseni capital province of Thronehold.⁠

Badelund is surrounded by high walls to protect the small peasant town from uninvited fey visitors. Feyfrost fey are notorious child-stealers. Badelund is the first village on the Frozen Road west of Isseld and hosts a number of inns and taverns to serve the tired merchants sailing the Frozen Road. Baroness Pavlina is the ruler of the town. Because of her kindness and her love for a peasant, Pavlina was sent to Badelund as a punishment. The Baroness and her Ulfen husband Oddvar Pavelsson are wise governors and do their best to make peasants' life bearable. It is well known that Pavlina sends mercenary groups north to retrieve stolen children. Such groups are the Home Again Safe led by Helena Oukarnion and the White Dawn Hunters led by Mikhail Shalanov.⁠
1148800200:
Three Pines Ford

Three Pines Ford is a sizable town nestled on the Tourondel River of Lastwall, east of the forest of Fangwood, and directly on its border with Nirmathas. It serves as a meeting-place for Lastwall officials and fresh recruits from Nirmathas. Heroes of Nirmathas use Three Pines Ford as a hiding place from agents of Molthune, due to the town's close proximity to the Nirmathi border.⁠
1168985690:
Blushing Rose

The Blushing Rose is the most successful brothel in Kaer Maga. Run by Rosaline Merithane, the establishment's influence is such that businesses throughout the district listen to Madam Rose's orders as if she were their boss. It faces increasingly fierce competition from the Strapping Lad, a rivalry that could escalate to violence.⁠
1180761240:
Devil's Nursery

The slums of Devil's Nursery, located in the Redroof neighborhood of Kintargo, are named for the large proportion of its residents who are cambions, most of whom fled here from less tolerant corners of Cheliax.⁠
1181952710:
Wilkesmont

Wilkesmont is a small town located inside the Shroudwood in the River Kingdom of Daggermark. The town was the home of the bandit lord Miklos Jakab, self-proclaimed ruler of the Shroudwood.

Jakab, the last serious bandit threat to Daggermark, was killed in 4566 AR; his followers swore fealty to Daggermark. Due to its location in the wood, the town is relatively cut off from the rest of the kingdom and an easy target whenever the Daggermark military fails to protect it. Wilkesmont has been burned to the ground three times, and each time has been rebuilt bigger than before. The town lacks any fortifications, relying on the heavy wood to keep most raiders away.

Recently, a bandit lord from Sevenarches boasted he will claim the Shroudwood, so the residents of Wilkesmont plan to use assassins from Daggermark to stop him.⁠
1185114930:
Whitemound

Whitemound is a town nestled in the foothills of the Mindspin Mountains, on the border between the Atteran Ranches and the Uthori Steppes in the far north of Nidal.⁠ The town boasts a thriving economy thanks to its granary and serves as a popular stop for ranchers to sell their produce or to hold ceremonies, such as weddings. It is also famous for its tanners' leather goods.⁠

Umbral Court agent Insevier of Nisroch is officially the town's leader, though this is more of a punishment imposed upon him due to several failed missions. The citizens of Whitemound generally avoid him, only interacting with him during sacred celebrations of Zon-Kuthon. Insevier is tasked with patrolling the Uthori Pass to prevent citizens from escaping to Korvosa, but in recent years he has not had much to do, as a leucrotta known as the Ascian, has been hunting down anyone attempting to cross, especially those from Whitemound.⁠
1187192820:
Pulura's Fall

Pulura's Fall is a former waterfall located in Sarkoris near the Sarkoris Scar, northeast of the ruins of Iz.⁠⁠ Maybe one of the only places not fully controlled by demons in the Wounded Lands while the Worldwound was open, a temple of Pulura led by the powerful cleric Eliandra stood in the dried-up waterfall.⁠
1189593300:
Pendaka

Pendaka is a tiny thorp located on a rocky promontory that overlooks Claybottom Lake's southern shore near where it flows into the Skull River. Pendaka has a single inn that also functions as a trading post known as the Walleyed Wife, but the settlement's only real claim to fame is its skilled baker, Olam Keecher, and his delicious cranberry turtle egg pies.⁠⁠
1195368040:
Slave Barge Dock

The Slave Barge Dock is the most used port on Parego Regicona, although in 4710 AR, a group of erinyes took control of it to use in their search for new victims.⁠
1196811420:
Cindermaw's Feeding Grounds

Cindermaw's Feeding Grounds are the ancient home of the purple worm Cindermaw. Located in the Cinderlands of Varisia, it is here that the Shoanti hero Skurak faced Cindermaw with only a dagger, was swallowed, and cut his way out from its fiery belly.⁠⁠
1203353310:
Humbolt's Outfitters
